Demonstrated experience designing experiences and user flows.
Strong understanding of user-centered design principles and best practices.
Ability to learn unfamiliar systems, form an understanding through independent research, and effectively work with a mentor and teammates.
Are a self-motivated problem solver committed to personal growth.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Proven ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate work while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs.
Ability to participate in a paid full-time internship between May–August, 2027. 
Preferred Qualifications (A bonus, not a requirement)
Previous project, internship, or work experience in UX/UI design or related fields.
Experience working with or conducting your own research, presenting results, and acting on those results.
Experience with AI tools like Cursor, Lovable, V0, or any others.
Strong knowledge in design craft and visual design.
Intent to return to the degree program after the completion of the internship/co-op.

postings.title: Software Engineer, Intern
postings.description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 
Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
What you'll do
As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous engineers in the industry and learn how to ship high-quality work at scale. By contributing to Stripe’s codebase you’ll work across domains that give you insight into how the global economy works. Recent intern projects include expanding Stripe’s Payments Foundation Model capabilities to improve generalized anomaly detection, building more approachable fraud controls, creating safer payouts, and developing user-facing solutions that prevent costly pricing mistakes and make merchant checkout setup easier.
Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.
Responsibilities
Operate as a real member of the team you join; engage in team discussions, decisions, and the technical design process.
Write software that will be used in production, and has meaningful impact to Stripe’s business and users.
Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews or design discussions
Collaborate with other engineers and cross-functional stakeholders to proactively seek and incorporate feedback.
Learn quickly by asking great questions, working with your intern manager and teammates effectively, communicating the status of your work clearly, and building with the latest AI tooling.
Who you are
Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. 
Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Minimum requirements
A strong fundamental understanding of computer science through pursuit of a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science, math, or a related discipline.
Experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Ruby, Java, Javascript, Go, and Scala. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present.
Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders.
Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor or subject matter experts.
Ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate development while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs.
Preferred qualifications
At least 1 year of university education, or equivalent work experience.
One or more areas of specialized knowledge (frontend, backend, infrastructure or other technologies) balanced with general skills and knowledge.
Experience writing high quality pull requests, with good test coverage, and working knowledge to complete projects with minimal defects.
Familiarity with navigating and managing your work in new code bases, with multiple languages.
Clear written communication skills, with the ability to write clearly to explain your work to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes.

Recent intern projects include expanding Stripe’s Payments Foundation Model capabilities to improve generalized anomaly detection, building more approachable fraud controls, creating safer payouts, and developing user-facing solutions that prevent costly pricing mistakes and make merchant checkout setup easier.
Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high. 
Responsibilities
Operate as a real member of the team you join; engage in team discussions, decisions, and the technical design process.
Write software that will be used in production, and has meaningful impact to Stripe’s business and users.
Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews or design discussions
Collaborate with other engineers and cross-functional stakeholders to proactively seek and incorporate feedback.
Learn quickly by asking great questions, working with your intern manager and teammates effectively, communicating the status of your work clearly, and building with the latest AI tooling.
Who you are
Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. 
Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Minimum requirements
A strong fundamental understanding of computer science through pursuit of a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science, math, or a related discipline. 
Experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Ruby, Java, Javascript, Go, and Scala. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present.
Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders.
Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor or subject matter experts. 
Ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate development while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs.
Preferred qualifications
At least 1 year of university education, or equivalent work experience.
One or more areas of specialized knowledge (frontend, backend, infrastructure or other technologies) balanced with general skills and knowledge. 
Experience writing high quality pull requests, with good test coverage, and working knowledge to complete projects with minimal defects.
Familiarity with navigating and managing your work in new code bases, with multiple languages.
Clear written communication skills, with the ability to write clearly to explain your work to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes.

postings.title: Applied Science Intern
postings.description:
As an Applied Science Intern, you will join a cross-functional team of engineers and applied scientists building AI-powered features within the Datadog platform. You will contribute to both existing and new products by improving machine learning models, developing new AI capabilities, and helping bring research into production. Working closely with engineering and product partners, you'll gain hands-on experience deploying AI systems at scale while strengthening your product mindset, collaboration, and communication skills. You'll also have opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that directly powers customer-facing features.
At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.
 
What You’ll Do:
Design solutions for AI use cases by researching and benchmarking state-of-the-art models to identify the best approach
Build highly scalable product features using generative AI, machine learning algorithms, and statistical techniques
Contribute to the development, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance of production AI models, services, and infrastructure
Explore, analyze, and derive insights from the large-scale observability data flowing through Datadog systems
Participate in technical knowledge sharing by presenting recent academic research and investigating emerging model architectures to improve existing and future products
Collaborate with engineering and product teams to productionize AI solutions and deliver customer-facing features
 
Who You Are:
You will graduate in 2027 with a degree in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field
You have experience building machine learning models through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects
You have strong programming skills and are eager to learn new languages and technologies
You communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
You have a strong interest in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data-driven product development
Available to complete a 6-month internship beginning in February, March, April, May, or June 2027 (we are unable to accommodate internships starting at any other time)
Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply.
 
Benefits and Growth:
Work on meaningful technical challenges alongside engineers across the globe
Participate in mentorship and buddy programs designed to support learning and development
Join an in-person intern cohort, attend company social events, and engage with Datadog Community Guilds and employee resource groups throughout the internship
Receive relocation support and travel benefits where applicable
Enjoy office perks including snacks, drinks, and catered lunches on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday
Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

postings.title: Research Science Intern (PhD)
postings.location: New York, New York, USA; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA
postings.description:
Datadog AI Research — Scholars Program with Carnegie Mellon University
Datadog AI Research (DAIR) is partnering with Carnegie Mellon University to support a small number of PhD students working on open research problems grounded by ongoing efforts at Datadog/DAIR. 
You will frame a problem, run your own experiments, and write up what you find, with compute and data at a scale most academic labs cannot provide.  You will collaborate with colleagues working on the same questions.
 
The Lab And The Research:
DAIR is an industrial research lab motivated by practical challenges in observability and software operation: detecting and diagnosing failures, understanding complex production environments, and helping engineers operate software more effectively. The lab focuses on creating specialized foundation models, post-training and evaluating AI agents, and building frontier-scale machine learning systems. By combining fundamental research with Datadog's large-scale, real-world data and infrastructure, the lab develops new AI capabilities and translates them into practical systems with meaningful impact.
Internship projects are shaped with your DAIR mentor and your CMU faculty advisor. You do not need prior experience with observability, monitoring, or infrastructure.
 
What You'll Do:
Own a research project end to end: framing the question, running the experiments, writing it up
Work directly with a DAIR mentor engaged in the same problem, and stay connected to your advisor and lab
Publish, and use the work toward your dissertation
See research reach production, when it works
 
Who You Are:
Currently enrolled in a PhD program at Carnegie Mellon in machine learning, computer science, statistics, or a related field
Depth in at least one area relevant to the research above
Comfort running real experiments — training models, working with GPUs, reading and reimplementing recent papers
Evidence you can do research: conference or workshop papers, preprints, open-source contributions, or a lab project you can discuss in depth
Research taste. You can explain why a problem matters and what would change if it were solved.
Honest empiricism. You report the ablation that didn't work.
Support from your faculty advisor.
 
Not Required:
A long publication record. How you think matters more than how much you've published.
Observability, monitoring, or SRE background.
A perfect match to the areas above.
 
Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply.
 
This job is available in various departments within our company; to conform to US export control regulations, some of these roles may require candidates to be eligible for any required authorizations from the US government.

postings.title: Drone Operations, Intern - Labs (Summer 2027)
postings.description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. The Drone Operations team keeps DoorDash's drones airworthy and operates them safely. Our missions range from experimental test flights to commercial delivery. We're hiring Drone Operations interns to work at the intersection of operations and robotics to solve key business problems with elegant technical solutions. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions to a service loved by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!
About the Role
As a Drone Operations Intern, you will support daily flight operations for DoorDash’s drone delivery program, from our test flight program to our commercial operation. You will get exposure to all elements of our operation, including Pilots, Maintenance Technicians, Quality/Safety, and Engineering. You will rotate around our facilities and get an end-to-end view of our program.  In your first 30 days, you will learn our flight procedures and safety practices. By 90 days, you will own a project that improves flight safety, reliability, or efficiency. Success means the team adopts your work and our operations measurably improve. It is an exciting time to join as we scale from test flights to commercial delivery.You will report into the Head of Drone Operations on our Drone Operations team in our Labs organization.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Work with pilots, technicians, and engineers to troubleshoot issues and improve procedures.
Review flight logs and mission data to find trends in safety, reliability, and delivery performance.
Help run field operations at flight sites, including aircraft setup, loading, and recovery.
Own an intern project and present your results to the team at the end of summer.
We’re excited about you because…
You are pursuing a B.S. or M.S. Degree in Aviation Studies or equivalent, have no more than 2 years of full-time work experience, and are graduating between Fall 2027 to Summer 2028.You are available for a May or June 2027 start date (Internships are only hosted during the Summer)
You hold, or are willing to obtain, a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate.
You have hands-on experience building, flying, or maintaining drones or radio-controlled (RC) aircraft.
You can operate in field environments with extended periods of standing, repetitive drone handling, and outdoor exposure to varying weather (heat, dust, cold, wind, etc.).
You communicate clearly and follow safety procedures carefully.
Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis
Compensation
The internship is 12 weeks long. The intern’s starting pay will fall within the weekly pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including education, work location, and market conditions. 
Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base pay, interns are eligible for both a housing stipend and relocation stipend. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being.  That’s why we offer our interns a wellness reimbursement benefit, access to an employee assistance program, in-office lunch credits and more!
Base Pay (Weekly)
$1,200 — $1,200 USD

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.
DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

postings.title: Electrical Engineer, Intern - Labs (Summer 2027)
postings.description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is DoorDash's autonomous delivery group, building the robots and hardware that move goods without a driver. The Vehicle Electrical team designs the electronics at the core of these systems, including power and motor-control electronics, charging, and the test benches that prove the whole system works.
About the Role
As a summer intern, you will own a defined hardware project in one of three areas: an on-board charger prototype, an in-house motor control circuit, or a full-power hardware test bench with motor power and battery simulation. You will take it from requirements through design, build, and bench validation, and present your results to the team at the end of the summer. You will report into the Director, Electrical Engineering in our DoorDash Labs organization.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own an end-to-end project in one of three areas: an on-board charger prototype, an in-house motor control circuit, or a full-power hardware test bench.
Design, build, and bring up hardware, from schematic and component selection through prototype assembly and debug.
Characterize your design on the bench with lab equipment, measuring efficiency, thermal, and control performance against requirements.
Collaborate with power electronics, firmware, and test engineers, and incorporate design review feedback into your work.
Document your results and present your findings to the team at the end of your internship.
We're excited about you because…
You are pursuing a B.S. or M.S. Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent, have no more than 2 years of full-time work experience, and are graduating between Fall 2027 to Summer 2028.
You are available for a May or June 2027 start date (Internships are only hosted during the Summer).
You have coursework or project experience in power electronics, including switch-mode converters (buck, boost, PFC, isolated DC-DC), gate drive, magnetics, and power-stage design.
You understand motor control fundamentals, including BLDC/PMSM drives, inverter half-bridges, field-oriented control, and current and position sensing.
You understand analog and feedback-control fundamentals, including op-amp sensing circuits, ADC signal conditioning, loop compensation, and stability analysis.
You can capture schematics and lay out PCBs in a tool such as Altium or KiCad, with awareness of high-current layout, thermal, and EMC considerations.
You understand lithium-ion battery charging (CC/CV profiles, protection limits) and how a battery management system interfaces with a charger or load.
You have hands-on lab experience with oscilloscopes, differential probes, power supplies, and electronic loads, and can safely debug high-current, high-voltage hardware.
You can write Python or C/C++ for instrument automation, data acquisition, or microcontroller bring-up.
You are able to work onsite at our Oakland, CA office.
Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis

postings.description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better 
About the Role
As a Mechanical Engineering Intern, you will work on all aspects of the mechanical design process, including design, analysis, prototyping, and validation of components and systems for DoorDash's next-generation autonomous delivery vehicle.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Design detailed components and sub-assemblies for a high-profile delivery robot, with the support of your mentor, manager, and team members.
Build production-quality 3D CAD models and drawings, and present your work in cross-functional design reviews.
Collaborate with electrical, systems, and manufacturing engineers to make sure your designs integrate cleanly and can be manufactured, assembled, and serviced at fleet scale.
Learn how to validate designs through prototype builds, bench testing, and tolerance and structural analysis, and act on feedback
We’re excited about you because…
You are pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering or a related field (such as Mechatronics, Robotics, Aerospace, or Automotive Engineering), have no more than 2 years of full-time work experience, and are available for a May or June 2027 start date (internships are only hosted during the summer).
You have hands-on experience with 3D CAD (such as NX, SolidWorks, or CATIA), preferably NX.
You have a solid grasp of engineering fundamentals and use first principles, calculations, simulation, and test data to support design decisions.
You have shown interest in mechanical design through coursework, team projects (such as Formula SAE or robotics clubs), or personal builds.
You can work independently on assigned design tasks and you want to learn how products are designed, built, and operated at scale.

postings.description:

DoorDash is building the world’s most reliable on-demand logistics engine for delivery! We’re looking for experienced engineers to join our fast-growing engineering team to help us develop a 24x7 global infrastructure system that powers DoorDash’s three-sided marketplace of consumers, merchants, and dashers.

This intern will report into a manager on the Assignment Engine team. We believe interns are essential to our mission of attracting and retaining top talent. During the 12 week Operations Research internship, interns will be completely immersed in their teams and will have the opportunity to develop, maintain & ship products. As an intern, you will directly impact our business by collaborating with your team to solve real problems for our customers.
Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. to be considered for this position. F-1 students are eligible if they are using Curricular Practical Training (CPT). DoorDash does not support students on J-1 visas at this time.

Have strong programming fundamentals, experience in object-oriented and/or functional programming languages, and a solid understanding of algorithms

Production experience with a JVM-based language (ie Java, Kotlin, Scala)
Experience with software development lifecycle (writing clean code, version control, unit testing, etc)

As a Product Design Intern, you’ll get to work on real projects that impact our customers, merchants, and Dashers. About Labs
DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We're hiring software engineer interns to work at the intersection of software engineering and robotics to solve key business problems with elegant technical solutions. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions to a service loved by millions of people, then we want to talk to you! 
About the Teams
We are hiring Software Engineer interns across our Perception, Autonomy Platform, and DoorDash Air Cloud (Foundry) team. Please review the team descriptions below to learn about each. Selected candidates will be notified of which team is interested in pursuing their candidacy. 
  Perception: The Perception team helps Dot understand the world through vision foundation models and VLMs, supported by lidar and radar for safety. We tackle rare scenarios, adverse weather, and advances in reinforcement learning and end-to-end driving to make deliveries faster and smoother. We're seeking exceptional engineers in machine learning, computer vision, and state estimation to turn cutting-edge research into profitable autonomous delivery.
Autonomy Platform: The Autonomy Platform team is responsible for the software foundation that Dot runs on. We build a wide variety of software frameworks for ensuring the robot operates reliably at an ever-increasing scale. This includes everything from designing the robot's operating system, building petabyte-scale data processing pipelines in the cloud, and optimizing nanosecond-level compute of bleeding-edge AI models. We are systems-oriented thinkers and hands-on builders who are excited to advance the state of the art in autonomy.

postings.title: Compiler Engineering Intern
postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
Join Us in Shaping the Future
At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.
The Team
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.
Position Overview
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.
Responsibilities
• Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
• Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
• Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
• Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
• Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
• Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications
• Currently pursuing a Bachelor or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline.
• Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area.
• Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems.
• Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions.
Preferred Qualifications
• Hands-on experience with LLVM or related compiler infrastructure, including front-end development, intermediate representations, optimization passes, code generation, runtimes, or debug information.
• Research or development experience involving CPU/GPU architectures, heterogeneous computing, AI/ML compilation, HPC, parallel programming, or performance optimization.
• Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.
• Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi.
• Tile-base programming model knowledge
• GPU Compute kernel writing experience
• Experience contributing to open-source software or working in a large collaborative codebase.
• Publications, technical reports, patents, open-source contributions, or other evidence of advanced technical work.
Success in This Role
• Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
• Clear written and verbal communication.
• Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.
• Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.

postings.title: Compiler Engineering Intern
postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software.
As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.
About the Team
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs.
The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models.
You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.
Position Overview
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on a scoped project that may involve:
Compiler features or MLIR-based intermediate representations
Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs)
Optimization, code generation, runtime, or offload support
Debug information or testing infrastructure
Performance analysis or developer tools
Projects may involve connecting software capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning models such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Kimi.
You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for an undergraduate student who wants to build practical compiler-engineering experience and apply foundational computer science concepts to production software.
Key Responsibilities
Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies
Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase
Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions
Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project
Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members
Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team
Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work

Clear written and verbal communication

postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
What if your next project helped power the future of technology?
At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. As an intern, you'll work side-by-side with industry leaders, gain hands-on experience on meaningful projects, and help solve real-world challenges that affect billions of people worldwide. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects.
What makes Intel unique is the opportunity to see the entire technology lifecycle in action. Unlike many companies where hardware, software, and manufacturing operate separately, Intel brings them together, giving you exposure to everything from research and design to advanced semiconductor manufacturing and global deployment.
Whether you're tackling engineering challenges, improving operations, analyzing data, advancing next-generation technologies, or supporting global customers, you'll build valuable skills while contributing to innovations that enable a more sustainable and connected future.
Bring your curiosity, make an impact, and see where your ideas can take you at Intel.
What You'll Do
The world's most advanced semiconductors depend on world-class facilities engineering. As a Facilities Services Intern, you'll support the critical infrastructure, systems, sustainability, and reliability behind Intel's manufacturing operations.
Support engineering projects and continuous improvement initiatives.
Analyze system and equipment performance to identify improvement opportunities.

postings.title: Compiler Engineering Graduate Intern
postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
Join Us in Shaping the Future
At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.
The Team
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.
Position Overview
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.
Responsibilities
• Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
• Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
• Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
• Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
• Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
• Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.
Success in This Role
• Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
• Clear written and verbal communication.
• Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.
• Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications
• Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline.
• Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area.
• Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems.
• Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions.
Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.
• Hands-on experience with LLVM or related compiler infrastructure, including front-end development, intermediate representations, optimization passes, code generation, runtimes, or debug information.
• Research or development experience involving CPU/GPU architectures, heterogeneous computing, AI/ML compilation, HPC, parallel programming, or performance optimization.
• Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning models such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Kimi.
• Tile-base programming model knowledge
• GPU Compute kernel writing experience
• Experience contributing to open-source software or working in a large collaborative codebase.
• Publications, technical reports, patents, open-source contributions, or other evidence of advanced technical work.

postings.title: AI Hardware Engineering Intern
postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
About the Job
Intel is seeking exceptional Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, and AI/ML students to join an AI Hardware Engineering internship focused on the future of AI inference and AI infrastructure with hardware/software co-design expertise.
This internship approaches AI infrastructure as a hardware/software co-design challenge. The intern will analyze how model architecture, inference behavior, memory movement, data-center constraints, and software stacks influence end-to-end customer outcomes, including throughput, latency, time-to-first-token, tokens per second, power consumption, utilization, total cost of ownership, and deployability.
The successful candidate will be technically hands-on, capable of independent research and analysis, and comfortable working within a highly technical team of researchers and engineers addressing complex AI hardware and infrastructure challenges.
What You Will Do
Conduct technical research on the next generation of AI infrastructure, including CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, ASICs, memory systems, networking, storage, rack-scale architecture, power delivery, cooling, and cluster management.
Analyze GenAI and agentic AI workloads to understand their hardware implications, including transformer architecture based inference, mixture-of-experts architectures, multimodal models, real-time interactive inference, and distributed serving.
Evaluate the hardware behavior of AI inference pipelines, including the distinct demands of prompt processing/prefill and token generation/decode, memory capacity, memory bandwidth, KV-cache management, compute utilization, interconnect bandwidth, and latency. For example, cluster architecture around optimizing both prefill and decode through hardware, memory, and system co-design.
Identify product and system gaps that may limit Intel's ability to serve AI customers effectively, including hardware capabilities, developer tooling, performance libraries, reference architectures, deployment models, observability, and ecosystem enablement.
- Expertise in modern high-performance CPU, GPU, or AI accelerator architecture and hardware/software interactions.
- Support Silicon HW programs through multiple phases of the silicon lifecycle, with end-to-end chip execution from concept to silicon.
- Good understanding with firmware codebases, compilers, kernels, serving stacks and model architectures.
- Familiar with driving silicon design for subsystems and/or top-level functions with ASICs and SOCs from an architecture specification to production silicon including memory subsystems and interconnects: scale up, scale out, scale across, power management , liquid cooling at rack scale level, deep system level observability & telemetry and dependent impact into Gen AI and LLM level performance/tco/execution KPIs
Develop technical recommendations for what Intel should build, optimize, enable, partner on to meet AI customer requirements based on deep understanding of customer use cases, workload performance, and ML systems research.
Benchmark and compare relevant AI hardware and infrastructure approaches across performance, power efficiency, cost, programmability, memory hierarchy, scalability, ecosystem maturity, and workload fit.
Develop technical models, simulations, prototypes, or analysis tools to evaluate hardware/software trade offs for AI workloads.
Investigate system bottlenecks across compute, memory, networking, storage, and software orchestration, and propose methods to improve end-to-end AI workload performance.
Work with Intel technical teams and external ISVs to collect data on model requirements, inference bottlenecks, deployment challenges, hardware optimization opportunities, and customer priorities.
Engage with AI software ecosystem partners, including model providers, inference-engine developers, cloud providers, framework teams, and ISVs, to understand how their stacks interact with underlying hardware.
Good understanding of modern AI software layers, including PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, model serving, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, Kubernetes, and Neocloud design efficiencies.
Present findings through architecture diagrams, benchmark analyses, technical reports, design recommendations, and executive-ready presentations.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications
Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, AI/ML, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Strong foundation in computer architecture, operating systems, distributed systems, parallel computing, AI/ML systems, high-performance computing, or systems software.
Familiarity with generative AI models and inference concepts, including transformers, attention, token generation, model serving, quantization, batching, KV cache, long-context workloads, and latency-throughput trade-offs.
Experience programming in one or more of the languages - C, C++, Rust, CUDA, SYCL, OpenCL, or a comparable low-level or performance-oriented language.
Strong academic performance with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher required.
Preferred Qualifications
Coursework, research, or project experience in computer architecture, VLSI, digital design, ASIC/FPGA systems, compilers, kernel development, GPU programming, distributed systems, high-performance computing, or AI systems.
Experience using profiling, tracing, or benchmarking tools to evaluate CPU, GPU, accelerator, network, memory, storage, or software performance.
Familiarity with AI hardware platforms such as Intel Xeon processors, Intel GPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, TPUs, custom AI accelerators, FPGAs, or domain-specific inference ASICs.
Understanding of memory hierarchies and performance concepts, including cache behavior, DRAM, HBM, memory bandwidth, memory capacity, latency, data locality, DMA, and data movement.
Experience with inference frameworks or runtimes such as vLLM, SGLang, Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch, Triton, or Ray.
Familiarity with AI systems infrastructure such as Linux, containers, Kubernetes, distributed storage, RDMA over Ethernet, InfiniBand, CXL, PCIe, NVMe, UALink/eSUN based interconnects, silicon photonics and cluster-management software.
Some experience with simulation, modeling, emulation, RTL, FPGA prototyping, firmware, driver development, or low-level debugging.
Some experience contributing to open-source systems, ML infrastructure, compiler, kernel, framework, or performance-engineering projects.

postings.title: GPU Architecture Graduate Intern
postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
The Role and Impact
As a Silicon Architecture Graduate Intern, you will contribute to the definition and architecture of cutting-edge silicon solutions, including hardware, firmware, and platform specifications. You will assist in modeling and simulation to analyze performance, power, and feature trade-offs across interconnected subsystems, guiding architectural decisions to meet product goals. In this role, you will collaborate with architects, design engineers, and validation teams to support the early-stage feasibility and specification development of innovative technologies.
Business Group
You will be part of the Data Center Group (DCG), a global organization dedicated to powering the world's digital infrastructure. The team focuses on developing highly scalable and efficient solutions to support Intel's leadership in advanced computing and data center technologies. Joining this group provides the opportunity to contribute to Intel's broader mission of enabling continued innovation in high-performance computing and data solutions.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist in defining silicon architecture specifications based on product requirements and feature integration.
- Support modeling and simulation tasks to evaluate performance, power, and trade-offs for architectural decisions.
- Collaborate with architects, design engineers, and validation teams to ensure feasibility and alignment with product goals.
- Contribute to the development of high-level models and tools for architectural analysis.
- Explore GPU concepts such as SIMT, parallelism, and cache hierarchies to guide architectural improvements.
- Apply programming skills in C, C++, and Python for prototyping and analysis tasks.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications
- Pursuing master's degree in GPU architecture, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or tightly related field.
- Knowledge of GPU architecture concepts, including SIMT, parallelism, and cache hierarchies.
- Proficiency in C, C++, and Python programming.
- Understanding of hardware pipelines and basic RTL design methodologies.
- 3.0 GPA
Preferred Qualifications
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills to address complex technical challenges.
- Excellent communication and teamwork abilities to thrive in a collaborative environment.
- Enthusiasm to learn and grow within Intel's innovative ecosystem, contributing to impactful technologies.
Ready to launch your career in silicon architecture? Join us to gain hands-on experience, expand your skills, and make an impact in shaping the future of computing technologies.

postings.title: Silicon Hardware Engineering - Intern, Bachelor’s
postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
What if your next project helped power the future of technology?
At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. You’ll work side-by-side with industry leaders, gain hands-on experience on meaningful projects, and help solve real-world challenges that affect billions of people worldwide. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects.
What makes Intel unique is the opportunity to see the entire technology lifecycle in action. Unlike many companies where hardware, software, and manufacturing operate separately, Intel brings them together, giving you exposure to everything from research and design to advanced semiconductor manufacturing and global deployment.
Whether you're tackling engineering challenges, improving operations, analyzing data, advancing next-generation technologies, or supporting global customers, you'll build valuable skills while contributing to innovations that enable a more sustainable and connected future.
Bring your curiosity, make an impact, and see where your ideas can take you at Intel.
What You'll Do
Build technologies that power the future of computing. As a Silicon Hardware Engineering Intern, you'll work on meaningful projects while building technical expertise that accelerates your professional growth.
Silicon architecture, circuit design, logic, layout, physical design, verification, validation, and debug.
Design, build, test, and analyze technologies at the core of Intel processors and platforms.
Use scripting, data analysis, and hardware validation methods to solve technical problems.
Collaborate across silicon, product, and manufacturing teams.
Contribute to innovations in processors, GPUs, SoCs, photonics, and validation systems.
Develop technical depth, tackle complex challenges, and contribute from day one while learning alongside experienced Intel engineers and technical leaders.
Where Your Career Could Take You
Potential opportunity areas include:
Analog Circuit Design Engineer
CPU/GPU Design Verification Engineer
GPU Physical Design Engineer
DFT Design Engineer
Formal Verification Engineer
Product Development Engineer

Silicon Product Architect
SoC Logic Design Engineer
Build technical expertise, explore new possibilities, and help shape what is next in computing and semiconductor technology.

Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related STEM field.
3+ months of experience gained through coursework, academic projects, research, internships, co-ops, student organizations, assistantships, or other relevant technical experiences.

GPA of 3.0 or higher preferred.
Experience or interest in design, architecture, programming, scripting, data analysis, automation, modeling, simulation, validation, or debugging.

Strong problem-solving, communication, collaboration, and ability to work in team-based environments.

postings.title: Module Engineering PhD Intern 2027
postings.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
As a Module Engineering Intern within Intel's F25 Metals organization, you will work alongside engineers, technicians, and operations teams to support High Volume Manufacturing (HVM) of Intel's leading-edge semiconductor technologies. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in semiconductor manufacturing while contributing to real-world engineering and operational challenges.
Interns will own and execute a meaningful project focused on areas such as process improvement, manufacturing efficiency, equipment performance, automation, data analytics, quality systems, or operational excellence. In addition to their primary project, interns will participate in day-to-day engineering activities and engage with cross-functional stakeholders to gain a broad understanding of semiconductor manufacturing operations.
Throughout the internship, you will learn how engineering decisions are made in a high-volume manufacturing environment by observing manufacturing workflows, analyzing data, identifying improvement opportunities, and communicating recommendations to technical and business partners. Interns are encouraged to explore multiple aspects of the organization through networking, mentorship, training, and collaboration across engineering disciplines.
This internship provides opportunities to:
Lead a project from problem definition through execution and final presentation
Analyze manufacturing, equipment, and operational data to support decision making
Apply structured problem-solving and continuous improvement methodologies
Collaborate with engineers, technicians, quality teams, and operational stakeholders
Develop technical communication and presentation skills
Gain exposure to advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies and operations
Successful candidates will demonstrate curiosity, initiative, strong problem-solving abilities, and a desire to learn in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. This role is designed to provide meaningful industry experience while helping evaluate potential future engineers for full-time opportunities within Intel.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications
Qualifications are typically obtained through a combination of academic coursework, research experience, internships, and/or relevant industry experience.
Currently pursuing a PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or a related technical discipline.
Minimum GPA of 3.0.
Academic coursework or research experience in semiconductor processing, materials science, microelectronics, advanced materials, or a closely related field.
Availability to participate in a minimum 10 to 12-week summer internship.
3+ months of educational, research, laboratory, internship, or industry experience.
Ability to work onsite in Hillsboro, Oregon.
Preferred Qualifications
Previous internship, research, laboratory, project, or industry experience in engineering, manufacturing, data analytics, process development, or a related technical field.
Familiarity with semiconductor manufacturing, industrial operations, quality systems, continuous improvement, or complex technical environments.
Experience working with data analysis and visualization tools such as Python, JMP, MATLAB, Power BI, Excel, SQL, or similar platforms.
Knowledge of problem-solving and continuous improvement methodologies such as root cause analysis, 8D, SPC, Pareto analysis, Design of Experiments (DOE), Lean, or Six Sigma.
Demonstrated ability to analyze data, identify trends, and develop data-driven recommendations.
Experience breaking down complex problems into executable plans and managing multiple priorities simultaneously.

Self-motivated with a demonstrated ability to learn quickly, ask questions, and take initiative in unfamiliar situations.

postings.title: 2027 Intern - Experience Researcher
postings.description:
The Opportunity
What does it take for the people who sell to and host Adobe's customers to do their best work? Which tools, technology, and spaces help them build strong customer relationships, and which ones slow them down? As an Experience Research Intern on the Workplace Digital Experiences team, you'll help us find out!
Our team designs and runs the technology behind how Adobe works together, from meeting spaces and customer briefing centers to Lab82, our workplace experimentation program. This summer, you'll lead a UX research project with Adobe's sales and customer-facing teams around the world, including our international markets, and turn what you learn into clear personas and needs. Your findings will help leaders decide where to invest, so you'll see your work shape real decisions!
All 2027 Adobe interns will be co-located hybrid. This means that interns will work between their assigned office and home. Interns will be based in the office where their manager and/or team are located, where they will get the most support to ensure collaboration and the best employee experience. Managers and their organization will determine the frequency they need to go into the office to meet priorities.

Plan and lead a research study, from research questions and recruiting through a final readout with leaders across Technology Services and Sales.
Conduct interviews, observation sessions, and a survey with sellers, solution consultants, and the teams who host customers.
Partner with our data analyst to compare what people tell you with usage and service data.
Build journey maps and personas, then turn them into a ranked list of opportunities, including concepts to test in Lab82.
Use Qualtrics, Miro, AI tools, and Adobe products to plan, analyze, and share your research.

Currently enrolled full time and pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Human-Computer Interaction, Information Science, Cognitive Science, Psychology, Anthropology, Design, or a related field, with an expected graduation date of December 2027 to June 2028.

Experience with qualitative research methods such as interviews, contextual inquiry, and synthesis, through coursework, projects, or internships.

Familiarity with survey design and basic quantitative analysis.
Clear writing and speaking skills, including turning research into stories that help people make decisions.
Curiosity and comfort working through open-ended problems with people across teams.
Interest in using AI tools to plan, analyze, and share research.

Adobe’s Enterprise Architecture & Emerging Technology team is part of Digital Employee Experience (DEX). We explore what’s next for how people work and turns the most promising ideas into something real. Our incubator looks at AI, data, and new ways of working to figure out what Adobe should build, test, and bet on next!
As an Emerging Technology & Innovation Intern, you will bring the perspective of someone entering the workforce just as it is being reinvented. You will own a prioritized emerging-tech challenge end-to-end: frame the problem, research it, generate ideas, prototype the strongest one, and present your findings to senior leaders. We will agree on the specific challenge together at the start of your internship so that it reflects the most relevant questions at that time and your own strengths and interests.
This is a role for an ideas person who is curious about where technology is headed, thinks in terms of people and problems rather than tools, and is eager to make ideas tangible. You will work alongside a team spanning architecture, AI, and incubation. You'll receivewit mentorship and visibility you rarely get this early in a career!
All 2027 Adobe interns will be co-located hybrid. This means that interns will work between their assigned office and home. Interns will be based in the office where their manager and/or team are located, where they will get the most support to ensure collaboration and the best employee experience. Managers and their organization will determine the frequency they need to go into the office to meet priorities.
What You'll Do
Research emerging technologies and trends in AI, data, and the future of work, and assess which matter most for Adobe
Use design thinking to frame problems, interview employees and partners, and uncover unmet needs
Generate and evaluate ideas, and make a clear case for the ones worth pursuing
Build quick, lightweight prototypes using AI tools, low-code approaches, or mock-ups to test ideas and make them tangible
Bring a fresh perspective on how the next generation of workers will expect to work, and challenge our assumptions
Share progress along the way and present findings and recommendations to leadership at the end of the internship
Leave behind something reusable: a prototype, framework, playbook, or set of design principles
What You Need to Succeed
Currently enrolled full-time and pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree or equivalent experience in computer science, information systems, design, human-computer interaction, data science, business, or a related field; or equivalent degree required with an expected graduation date of December 2027– June 2028
Strong working knowledge of AI: you use it regularly, understand what it can and can’t do, and have a point of view on where it is headed
Familiarity with design thinking or human-centered design, including research, ideation, and prototyping
Genuine curiosity and an ideas-first mentality, with the ability to spot patterns and imagine what could be
Comfort with ambiguity: you can take an open-ended problem, define it, and move it forward
Innovative problem-solving skills driven by data analysis
You should have hands-on ability to prototype and test ideas using intelligent automation platforms or visual development environments. Mock-ups are also acceptable. Having a project or experiment with AI to show us is a plus.
Ability to explain complex ideas clearly to non-technical audiences, in writing and in person
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with ability to work with people at all levels
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced dynamic environment

Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity.

postings.description:
The Opportunity
Adobe Researchers and Applied Scientists are building the next generation of advanced technologies and user experiences, creating new forms of creativity, freeing people from routine tasks, and helping enterprises understand and act quickly on customer and business insights. Our teams publish in leading journals and conferences, partner with product teams to ship high-profile features, and explore new product opportunities across a wide range of domains. Audio

postings.description:
The Opportunity
The Digital Strategy Group (DSG) works with C-level leadership at Adobe's top customers to craft strategies for customer-experience transformation and digital innovation. As part of our Strategic Advisory team, you'll partner directly with customers to define bold digital visions, align executive leadership, and build the transformation roadmaps that elevate and transform our customers' digital experience.
What You'll Do
Take part in client-facing strategy engagements for customers. In each engagement, you'll join a dedicated team working to solve our customers' biggest digital transformation challenges. You'll work cross-functionally with sales, marketing, product experts, and enterprise architects to deliver value for customers. We seek candidates who can contribute in one or more of the
following areas:
Leverage data, research, and industry insights to help customers understand the current state of their digital experience and how their own customers experience their digital platforms
Partner with customers to define bold digital visions, align executive leadership, and build transformation roadmaps that drive business outcomes
Lead the development of innovation and discovery workshops that bring cross-functional stakeholders together to align on business priorities, surface challenges, and co-create transformation opportunities
Translate customer goals and pain points into prioritized use cases and a sequenced roadmap for Adobe investment
Drive high-value opportunities end-to-end, from account planning and qualification through deal closure
Develop as a business leader! You'll learn about a wide range of Adobe products as you collaborate with people across Sales, Marketing, Product, and Professional Services. The Digital Strategy Group supports clients across the following industries: Retail & Consumer Goods, High Tech & Manufacturing, Financial Services & Insurance, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Communications, Media & Travel, and Public Sector. You'll complete a survey close to your start date to determine your industry team, where you'll deepen your subject matter expertise as you execute strategy engagements.
What You Need to Succeed
Currently enrolled full time and pursuing an MBA, graduating between December 2027 and June 2028
Ability to participate in a full time internship between May - September 2027
Outstanding record of academic achievement
Interest in business strategy, technology, or experience design through coursework, extracurricular activities or work/internship experience
Proven analytical and quantitative problem-solving skills, including independently conducting research, analyzing data, developing hypotheses, and synthesizing recommendations
Experience engaging and influencing senior stakeholders, including executives
Ability to communicate sophisticated ideas and craft strong narratives both verbally and in writing
Ability to project manage multiple moving parts simultaneously, navigate ambiguity, and lead cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment

Experience creating digital/brand/media strategies along with a practical understanding of the technologies and tactics necessary for execution

postings.description:
Internship Details
Location: London
Duration: 13 months
Start date: 1st July 2027
End date: 31st July 2028
Eligibility: You’re currently an undergraduate pursuing your Bachelor's degree on your penultimate year of study, looking for a placement year/sandwich year - Graduating in 2029
Hybrid: 3 days per week in the office, 2 days per week work from home
Annual Pay: £32,000
About the role
Curious about tech but not sure what sales really means? You’re not alone—and that’s exactly why this internship exists.
You will join our Adobe Sales Academy as a Business Development Representative Intern - our development programme designed to help you build the skills and confidence to thrive in tech sales. In this role, you focus on generating new leads, (both inbound and outbound), as well as qualify and nurture opportunities through the early stages of the buyer’s journey. As a Business Development Representative, you are a critical part of the sales ecosystem supporting your account team and customers.
This role equips you with a fantastic foundation to progress to many other opportunities throughout the sales organisation.
This isn’t just an internship—it’s your gateway into the world of innovation, customer engagement, and cutting-edge technology. At Adobe, we’re committed to nurturing the next generation of sales professionals—and that journey begins with you. This program includes hands-on mentorship, immersive training from Adobe Sales Academy and seasoned BDRs, practicing through role plays, and access to developmental courses developed to strengthen your professional and communication skills.
What you will do
As a Business Development Representative (BDR) Intern you'll be part of the team that helps Adobe connect with customers at the start of their buying journey. You will be the first point of contact for people interested in our products - guiding them, asking smart questions, and helping them figure out what they need. You'll qualify these opportunities ready to be passed over to our Field Sales Executives.
This includes target market penetration, calling on senior-level executives, following up on marketing-generated leads, webinar and event follow-up, and more.
Begin with shadowing your mentor, progress to practicing through role plays and guided activities, and eventually take on more responsibility by contacting customers and leading conversations yourself.
Start conversations with people who’ve shown interest in Adobe—through events, webinars, or marketing campaigns.
Reach out to decision-makers (yes, even senior execs!) and help them understand how Adobe’s tools—like Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, and Marketing Cloud—can support their goals.
Spot opportunities and pass them on to our sales team so they can take things further.
Work closely with teammates across sales, marketing, and operations to keep things moving and make sure everyone’s in the loop.
Hit your goals for generating leads and building pipeline—don’t worry, we’ll support you every step of the way.
Grow your skills in communication, teamwork, and business—while staying true to Adobe’s values and inclusive culture. This includes participating in structured training sessions, practicing through real-world role plays, and developing both sales-specific and professional skills that will set you up for long-term success.
What you need to succeed
We’re not looking for perfection—we’re looking for potential. If you’re curious, motivated, and ready to learn, you’re already off to a great start.
You’re comfortable working towards goals and enjoy seeing results.
You’ve shown drive—whether that’s through university projects, part-time work, volunteering, or anything where you’ve gone above and beyond.
You’re a confident communicator and can write clearly and professionally.
You’re organised, detail-oriented, and a good listener.
You’re tech-savvy and keen to learn how digital tools can solve real-world problems.

postings.description:
The Company
PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.
We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.
We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.
Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.
Job Summary:
MLE PhD Intern plays a critical role in ensuring PayPal’s adherence to a complex and evolving landscape of local and global regulations. By leveraging advanced machine learning, cutting-edge research, and data-driven insights, we design innovative solutions that streamline compliance processes, strengthen risk mitigation, and empower PayPal to deliver a secure, trusted, and seamless financial experience worldwide.
Job Description:
As a Machine Learning Engineer PhD Intern, you will work with experienced engineers, data scientists, and product teams to research, develop, and evaluate machine learning solutions. You’ll take on complex technical problems, work with large datasets, and contribute to model development and deployment. You should be comfortable applying advanced machine learning knowledge, communicating your findings, and collaborating to bring solutions into PayPal products and services.

Conduct applied research to identify and develop machine learning solutions for complex business challenges.
Design, build, and evaluate machine learning models, using appropriate methods to assess their effectiveness, reliability, and suitability for use.
Analyze data and conduct experiments to generate insights and guide model development.
Collaborate with engineers, data scientists, and cross-functional partners to translate business needs into scalable machine learning solutions.
Contribute to the development and deployment of machine learning pipelines and solutions in production environments.
Monitor model performance and identify opportunities to improve outcomes, reliability, and efficiency.
Document research, experiments, and technical decisions, and communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences.
Stay informed about developments in machine learning and assess their potential relevance to PayPal’s products and services.

Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, or a related field.
Strong foundation in machine learning and statistics, with research experience developing and evaluating models.
Proficiency in Python and experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or scikit-learn.
Strong analytical, communication, and collaboration skills. Relevant research publications are preferred.

Currently pursuing a PhD degree in computer science, machine learning, data science, computer engineering, or a related technical field at an accredited college or university.
